reason: Gravitational focusing helped planetesimals grow into a core in the previous chapter, so it is a plausible way to start building rocky embryos.
expectation: The rocky planetesimals will gather into a growing rocky body.

effect: Gravitational focusing was not the direct partner; crossing orbits automatically produced accreting planetary embryos.
reaction: The compatibility feedback made the failed guess productive.
reason: Gravitational focusing could help the new embryos gather more material, as it did for the outer core.
expectation: The embryos will grow by attracting more rocky material.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced a strongly attracting embryo, suggesting it can now gather material toward young Earth.
reaction: The connection between greater mass and faster accretion is satisfying.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock is a plausible source of the young Earth's volatile material.
expectation: The embryo will incorporate hydrated rock and gain volatile material.

effect: The embryo first collected rocky fragments to become proto-Earth; it has not yet incorporated the water-bearing rock.
reaction: The automatic correction clarified the order of growth.
reason: The rocky proto-Earth can plausibly incorporate the available hydrated asteroid material to become volatile-bearing.
expectation: Proto-Earth will gain volatile material from the hydrated rock.

effect: Proto-Earth has incorporated hydrated material, though that does not mean it has a surface ocean. The other rocky embryo still needs to grow.
reaction: The distinction between hydrated material and an ocean is useful.
reason: The accreting embryos are the likely starting point for the remaining goal, but their next partner is not clear.
expectation: The inspection will reveal how to grow another embryo.

effect: The inspection automatically grew Theia and completed the other embryo goal; proto-Earth still needs development.
reaction: The automatic growth was a useful result of checking compatibility.
reason: The hot, layered planetesimal may supply differentiated material to the hydrated proto-Earth, though the exact recipe is uncertain.
expectation: Proto-Earth will incorporate more material and progress toward the volatile-bearing young Earth.

effect: The hydrated proto-Earth currently has no available combination, so the remaining material may need preparation first.
reaction: The failed guess leaves the next step uncertain.
reason: Collisions could break the layered planetesimal into material that proto-Earth can incorporate.
expectation: The collision will produce fragments from the layered body.

effect: The collision exposed metallic core fragments, which may provide the missing material for proto-Earth.
reaction: The distinction between core fragments and rocky-layer fragments is useful.
reason: Proto-Earth may now be able to incorporate the newly exposed metal fragments.
expectation: Proto-Earth will incorporate metal and progress toward the remaining goal.

effect: The exposed core fragments supplied the metal needed to make a volatile-bearing young Earth, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the preparation pay off, and useful to learn that the timing and sources of Earth's hydrogen remain debated.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking the layered planetesimal to expose its core, then incorporating those fragments, connected differentiation with Earth's growth and completed the goal.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the intact layered planetesimal with proto-Earth was an unsuccessful guess; the result gave little direction beyond showing that the hydrated Earth had no available combination yet.

surprise.text: Hydrated rock did not imply a cool planet or a surface ocean, and metal and hydrogen-bearing material need not arrive in a fixed order.

arbitrary.text: The required order initially felt unclear: the strongly attracting embryo had to collect rocky fragments before it could take the hydrated rock. The feedback revealed the route, though the later explanation says accretion has no universal metal-first order.

continue.text: I would continue: the distinction between hydrated rock and an ocean, and the introduction of a hypothetical Theia, make me curious how the story reaches the Moon and a sea.
